jurisdictions.mayorSelectionNote: In Mayor-Council cities, Mayor is directly elected at-large (4-yr term; holds veto overridden by 2/3 council; § 50-608). In Council-Manager cities, council selects mayor from own membership as presiding chair (§ 50-809).
jurisdictions.electionAdministrationCitation: Idaho Code § 34-1401 (County clerk conducts all elections within county on consolidated dates)
jurisdictions.electionCostRule: Pro-rata reimbursement of direct election expenses to county
jurisdictions.recallCitation: Idaho Code Title 34 Ch. 17 (§ 34-1701 et seq.)
jurisdictions.recallMechanics: THE IDAHO RETENTION BARRIER (Idaho Code § 34-1712): Recall is NOT effective unless: (1) A majority votes YES on recall, AND (2) The number of YES votes equals or exceeds the total number of votes cast for the officer at their original election!
jurisdictions.initiativeNotes: Petition signed by 20% of registered electors. Council must either pass ordinance within 30 days or submit to voters at next general city election.
jurisdictions.referendumNotes: Petition signed by 20% of electors filed within 30 days suspends ordinance until voted upon.

jurisdictions.homeRuleAuthority: Ill. Const. Art. VII § 6; 65 ILCS 5 (Illinois Municipal Code)
jurisdictions.ballotCitation: 10 ILCS 5/Art. 7, Art. 10; 65 ILCS 5/3.1-25-20 (Partisan in aldermanic/village unless opted nonpartisan; strictly nonpartisan in Commission/Manager forms)
jurisdictions.electionTimingCitation: 10 ILCS 5/2A-1.1, 5/2A-1.2 (Consolidated Primary on last Tuesday in February; Consolidated Election on first Tuesday in April of odd-numbered years)
jurisdictions.runoffCitation: 65 ILCS 5/4-3-5, 65 ILCS 20/21-12 (In nonpartisan forms and Chicago, primary eliminates all but top two candidates who contest the April election)
jurisdictions.seatStructureDefault: two_aldermen_per_ward (Statutory cities: 65 ILCS 5/3.1-20-10) / at-large (Villages: 6 Trustees)
jurisdictions.mayorSelectionNote: Direct election in all forms (Mayor in cities, President in villages). Holds veto over council ordinances (overridden by 2/3 vote; 65 ILCS 5/3.1-40-45).
jurisdictions.electionAdministrationCitation: 10 ILCS 5/Art. 6 (County Clerk or Board of Election Commissioners conducts all consolidated elections)
jurisdictions.electionCostRule: Proportionate share billed to municipality under 10 ILCS 5/17-30
jurisdictions.recallCitation: 65 ILCS 5 (Absent in general law; Illinois courts hold recall unauthorized without express statute)
jurisdictions.recallMechanics: PROHIBITED under general law. Specific statutory recall exists ONLY for Chicago Mayor (added 2018; 10 ILCS 5/Art. 21A; requiring 15% registered voters in every ward) and Commission form (65 ILCS 5/4-7-1; 25% electors).
jurisdictions.initiativeNotes: Citizen initiative for ordinary municipal ordinances is PROHIBITED. Voter initiative permitted only on structural questions: adopting home rule, altering council size, or changing form of government (Ill. Const. Art. VII § 6(f)).
jurisdictions.referendumNotes: Protest referendum against general city ordinances is not authorized. Referenda are limited to back-door referendum questions on municipal bond issues and tax levy increases.

jurisdictions.homeRuleAuthority: Ind. Code Title 36; Ind. Code § 36-1-3 (Home Rule Act)
jurisdictions.ballotCitation: IC § 3-10-6-1, § 3-10-6-2 (MANDATORY PARTISAN ELECTIONS: candidates run in party primaries in May; general election in November of odd-numbered years)
jurisdictions.electionTimingCitation: IC § 3-10-6-5 (First Tuesday after first Monday in November of odd-numbered years; e.g. 2023, 2027)
jurisdictions.runoffCitation: IC § 3-12-8 (Plurality election in both primary and general elections; no runoffs)
jurisdictions.seatStructureDefault: hybrid_districts_and_at_large (2nd Class: 6 districts + 3 at-large; 3rd Class: 5 districts + 2 at-large)
jurisdictions.mayorSelectionNote: Direct election in all 2nd and 3rd class cities (4-yr term, full executive administration, veto power overridden by 2/3 council; IC § 36-4-5). In towns, Town Council selects Council President as executive head.
jurisdictions.electionAdministrationCitation: IC § 3-10-6-8 (County Election Board conducts municipal elections in all cities)
jurisdictions.electionCostRule: 100% apportioned and billed to municipality under IC § 3-5-3-8
jurisdictions.vacancyCitation: IC § 3-13-8-1 et seq. (Cities), IC § 3-13-9-1 et seq. (Towns)
jurisdictions.recallCitation: Ind. Code Title 36; Ind. Const. Art. 6
jurisdictions.recallMechanics: Municipal recall is STRICTLY PROHIBITED in Indiana. Officials can only be removed via judicial impeachment for official misconduct under IC § 5-8-1-35.
jurisdictions.initiativeNotes: Citizen initiative for municipal ordinances is STRICTLY PROHIBITED. The Indiana Home Rule Act expressly prohibits municipalities from creating direct legislative mechanisms.
jurisdictions.referendumNotes: Citizen protest referendum on city ordinances is PROHIBITED. Voter referenda exist only for public school capital projects and controlled municipal capital project tax caps.

jurisdictions.homeRuleAuthority: Kan. Const. Art. 12 § 5 (Home Rule Amendment); K.S.A. Ch. 12
jurisdictions.ballotCitation: K.S.A. § 25-2113 ('All elections for city officers shall be nonpartisan')
jurisdictions.electionTimingCitation: K.S.A. § 25-2107 (Consolidated Primary in August; General Election on first Tuesday after first Monday in November of odd-numbered years)
jurisdictions.runoffCitation: K.S.A. § 25-2120 (Plurality election; candidate with greatest number of votes elected; August primary held only if > 3 candidates file per seat)
jurisdictions.seatStructureDefault: single_member_wards (1st/2nd class mayor-council) / at-large (commission forms)
jurisdictions.mayorSelectionNote: Direct election in Mayor-Council cities (veto power in 1st class cities; overridden by 2/3 council). In commission-manager cities, mayor chosen by commissioners from own membership (K.S.A. § 12-1007).
jurisdictions.electionAdministrationCitation: K.S.A. § 25-2110 (County Election Officer conducts all municipal elections)
jurisdictions.electionCostRule: Pro-rata share billed by county to city under K.S.A. § 25-2201
jurisdictions.recallCitation: Kan. Const. Art. 4 § 3; K.S.A. § 25-4301 et seq. (Kansas Recall Act)
jurisdictions.recallMechanics: Strict grounds requirement certified by county attorney or district court before petition circulation. High signature threshold: 40% of votes cast for that office at last general election. Standalone Yes/No ballot.
jurisdictions.initiativeNotes: Petition signed by 25% (in 2nd/3rd class) or 40% (in 1st class) of qualified electors. Governing body must pass ordinance without alteration within 20 days or submit to election.
jurisdictions.referendumNotes: Protest referendum is guaranteed by constitution against CHARTER ORDINANCES (10% electors within 60 days suspends ordinance; Kan. Const. Art. 12 § 5(c)(3)).

jurisdictions.homeRuleAuthority: Ky. Const. §§ 156b, 160; KRS Ch. 67A, 67C, 83A
jurisdictions.ballotCitation: KRS 83A.050 (Nonpartisan default for cities; city may opt by ordinance to conduct partisan elections; Louisville Metro is PARTISAN under KRS 67C.103)
jurisdictions.electionTimingCitation: Ky. Const. § 148; KRS 118.025 (Primary on third Tuesday in May; General Election on first Tuesday after first Monday in November of even-numbered years)
jurisdictions.runoffCitation: KRS 83A.170 (Nonpartisan primary in May eliminates all but top two candidates who advance to November general election; plurality wins in November)
jurisdictions.seatStructureDefault: pure_at_large (statutory forms) / hybrid (LFUCG: 12 districts + 3 at-large; Louisville Metro: 26 single-member districts)
jurisdictions.mayorSelectionNote: Direct election in all forms (4-yr term). Strong Mayor with full executive administration and veto in Mayor-Council (KRS 83A.130), LFUCG (Charter Sec. 5.02), and Louisville Metro (KRS 67C.105). Weak/presiding mayor in Commission and Manager forms.
jurisdictions.electionAdministrationCitation: KRS 117.035 (County Board of Elections conducts all municipal and metro elections)
jurisdictions.electionCostRule: Pro-rata cost share paid by city to county treasury under KRS 117.345
jurisdictions.recallMechanics: Political recall is PROHIBITED for general elected municipal officers under Ky. Const. §§ 150 and 152. Limited statutory recall exists ONLY for protesting property tax rate increases exceeding the 4% revenue limit under KRS 132.017.
jurisdictions.initiativeNotes: Authorized ONLY in Commission and City Manager forms (petition signed by 20-25% of voters at last general election). Barred in LFUCG and Louisville Metro charters.
jurisdictions.referendumNotes: Authorized in Commission and City Manager forms (20% voter petition within 30 days suspends ordinance). Barred in LFUCG and Louisville Metro charters.

jurisdictions.homeRuleAuthority: La. Const. Art. VI § 5; La. R.S. Title 33
jurisdictions.ballotCitation: La. R.S. 18:401 et seq. (Louisiana Open Jungle Primary: all candidates appear on same primary ballot regardless of party affiliation)
jurisdictions.electionTimingCitation: La. R.S. 18:402 (Spring dates in presidential years, or fall dates in gubernatorial off-years)
jurisdictions.runoffCitation: La. R.S. 18:511 (Candidate receiving majority of votes cast in primary is elected; if no candidate clears 50%, top two advance to general election runoff 4 weeks later)
jurisdictions.seatStructureDefault: pure_at_large (Lawrason towns < 10,000) / single_member_districts (cities > 10,000: La. R.S. 33:382)
jurisdictions.mayorSelectionNote: Direct popular election across all forms (4-yr term). Mayor holds veto under Lawrason Act (overridden by 2/3 of aldermen; La. R.S. 33:404).
jurisdictions.electionAdministrationCitation: La. R.S. Title 18 (Parish Registrar of Voters and Parish Board of Election Supervisors conduct elections on state-owned voting machines)
jurisdictions.electionCostRule: State pays majority of costs; municipality pays proportional share under La. R.S. 18:1400.1
jurisdictions.recallCitation: La. Const. Art. X § 26; La. R.S. Title 18 Ch. 6-C (§ 18:1300.1 et seq.)
jurisdictions.recallMechanics: Universal statutory right. Tiered thresholds: 40% (<1,000 voters), 33.3% (1k-25k), 25% (25k-50k), 20% (>=50k). Standalone Yes/No recall election; if recalled, seat is declared vacant and filled under normal vacancy rules.
jurisdictions.initiativeNotes: Citizen ordinance initiative is NOT authorized in Lawrason Act municipalities; available ONLY where explicitly granted in individual Home Rule Charters (e.g. New Orleans, Baton Rouge).
jurisdictions.referendumNotes: Protest referendum is absent under general municipal law; referendum exists only where specified by charter or for local tax millage renewals.

jurisdictions.homeRuleAuthority: Mass. Const. Amend. Art. 89 (Home Rule Amendment); M.G.L. c. 43B
jurisdictions.ballotCitation: M.G.L. c. 43 § 15; c. 53 (Nonpartisan in towns and all Faulkner plans except Plan F which allows partisan primaries)
jurisdictions.electionTimingCitation: M.G.L. c. 39 § 9 (Town meetings held in spring between Feb 1 and May 31); M.G.L. c. 43 § 15 (Cities hold municipal elections on first Tuesday after first Monday in November of odd-numbered years)
jurisdictions.runoffCitation: M.G.L. c. 43 § 44D, c. 54 § 85 (Plurality default; in cities with preliminary nonpartisan elections, top two advance to November)
jurisdictions.seatStructureDefault: pure_at_large (Towns: Select Board 3 or 5 members) / hybrid (Cities: ward councillors + at-large councillors)
jurisdictions.mayorSelectionNote: Direct election in Faulkner Plan A and modern city charters (Strong Mayor with executive appointments and veto overridden by 2/3 council; c. 43 § 55). In Plan D/E, Council elects mayor as ceremonial chair.
jurisdictions.electionAdministrationCitation: M.G.L. c. 54 (Town/City Clerk and Board of Registrars of Voters administer municipal elections locally)
jurisdictions.electionCostRule: 100% municipal responsibility
jurisdictions.recallCitation: M.G.L. c. 43 (Absent in general law; exists only in special legislative charters)
jurisdictions.recallMechanics: Recall is absent under general Massachusetts law. A municipality can obtain recall only by petitioning the General Court (state legislature) for a special act charter.
jurisdictions.initiativeNotes: Under Faulkner Act, petition signed by 8% (regular election) or 12% (special election) of registered voters submitted to city council. If council fails to enact within 20 days, placed on ballot. In towns, 10 voters petition warrant article.
jurisdictions.referendumNotes: Under Faulkner Act, petition signed by 12% of registered voters filed within 20 days of ordinance passage suspends ordinance until council repeals or voters ratify.

jurisdictions.homeRuleAuthority: Md. Const. Art. XI-E; Md. Code Ann., Local Gov't (LG) Div. II
jurisdictions.ballotCitation: Md. Code Local Gov't § 4-108; Charters (Municipal elections nonpartisan in 156 of 157 municipalities; Baltimore City is PARTISAN)
jurisdictions.electionTimingCitation: Md. Code Local Gov't § 4-108 (Each municipality fixes election dates by charter; commonly May, June, or November)
jurisdictions.runoffCitation: Local Charters (Plurality default; candidate with greatest votes elected; Takoma Park uses Ranked-Choice Voting)
jurisdictions.seatStructureDefault: pure_at_large (small towns) / single_member_districts (larger cities)
jurisdictions.mayorSelectionNote: Direct election in Mayor-Council charters (Annapolis, Salisbury). Council-selected or weak mayor in Council-Manager charters.
jurisdictions.electionAdministrationCitation: Md. Code Local Gov't § 4-108 (Municipal Board of Supervisors of Elections administers local contests; county provides voter registry list)
jurisdictions.electionCostRule: 100% municipal responsibility
jurisdictions.vacancyCitation: Local Municipal Charters; Md. Code Local Gov't § 4-108
jurisdictions.recallCitation: Md. Const. Art. XI-E; Md. Code Local Gov't
jurisdictions.recallMechanics: Municipal recall is absent in general state law. Available only if explicitly authorized in a municipal charter.
jurisdictions.initiativeNotes: Citizen initiative is authorized ONLY for proposing municipal charter amendments (petition signed by 20% of qualified voters under LG § 4-305). General ordinance initiative is not authorized under state law.
jurisdictions.referendumNotes: Mandatory protest referendum applies to charter amendments passed by council (20% voter petition within 40 days forces referendum). Protest referendum on general ordinances exists where provided by charter.

jurisdictions.homeRuleAuthority: Maine Const. Art. VIII-A; 30-A M.R.S. § 2101 et seq. (Home Rule Act)
jurisdictions.ballotCitation: 30-A M.R.S. § 2528 (Town elections nonpartisan; Secret ballot / Australian ballot system)
jurisdictions.electionTimingCitation: 30-A M.R.S. § 2521 (Annual town meeting held in March or April; Cities frequently coordinate with November even-year election under Title 21-A)
jurisdictions.runoffCitation: 30-A M.R.S. § 2528 (Plurality election; candidate with greatest number of votes elected; Ranked-Choice Voting authorized for local adoption in charters, e.g. Portland)
jurisdictions.seatStructureDefault: pure_at_large (Towns: Select Board elected at-large with staggered 3-year terms: 30-A M.R.S. § 2526)
jurisdictions.mayorSelectionNote: In towns, Select Board elects chair. In cities, Mayor is directly elected or chosen by council; administrative power resides in City Manager unless Strong Mayor charter enacted.
jurisdictions.electionAdministrationCitation: 30-A M.R.S. § 2528; 21-A M.R.S. § 601 et seq. (Town/City Clerk conducts local elections)
jurisdictions.electionCostRule: 100% municipal responsibility
jurisdictions.recallMechanics: Authorized in towns by local ordinance (30-A M.R.S. § 2602(6)). Requires petition signed by 10% of votes cast in last gubernatorial election. Town holds special recall election.
jurisdictions.initiativeNotes: Petition signed by 10% of voters (or 10 voters in small towns) MANDATES Select Board to insert proposed article into the warrant for next Town Meeting.
jurisdictions.referendumNotes: Towns using referendum ballot system may petition ordinances to vote; charter cities define protest referendum by charter.

jurisdictions.homeRuleAuthority: Mich. Const. Art. VII § 22; Home Rule City Act (MCL 117.1 et seq.)
jurisdictions.ballotCitation: MCL 168.644e (Nonpartisan default in Home Rule cities; Fourth Class cities may conduct partisan elections)
jurisdictions.electionTimingCitation: MCL 168.644a (Odd-year November consolidated municipal elections; cities may adopt resolution/charter to hold elections in even-numbered years)
jurisdictions.runoffCitation: MCL 168.644f (Plurality election; nonpartisan primary held in August if more than twice the number of candidates file for a seat)
jurisdictions.seatStructureDefault: pure_at_large (Council-Manager cities) / single_member_districts (Detroit, Flint)
jurisdictions.mayorSelectionNote: Direct election in Mayor-Council charters (Detroit: strong mayor with full appointment and veto power). In Council-Manager charters (Grand Rapids, Ann Arbor), mayor is council chair directly elected or selected by council.
jurisdictions.electionAdministrationCitation: MCL 168.23 et seq. (City or Township Clerk conducts elections; City Board of Election Commissioners sets up voting precincts)
jurisdictions.electionCostRule: 100% municipal/township responsibility
jurisdictions.recallCitation: Mich. Const. Art. II § 8; MCL 168.951 et seq.
jurisdictions.recallMechanics: Universal constitutional right. Clarity hearing before county election commission. Petitions require 25% of the total votes cast in the electoral district for Governor in the last election. Recall election is a replacement election: incumbent automatically on ballot unless declining.
jurisdictions.initiativeNotes: Home Rule City Act mandates that each charter may provide for initiative and referendum. Commonly 10-15% of registered electors. Council must adopt or submit to voters.
jurisdictions.referendumNotes: Charter-authorized protest referendum suspends ordinance pending vote if filed within statutory/charter window.

jurisdictions.homeRuleAuthority: Minn. Const. Art. XII § 4; Minn. Stat. Ch. 410 (Home Rule) & Ch. 412 (Statutory Cities)
jurisdictions.ballotCitation: Minn. Stat. § 205.07, § 205.17 ('The municipal ballot shall be nonpartisan')
jurisdictions.electionTimingCitation: Minn. Stat. § 205.07 (Consolidated with statewide even-year general election on first Tuesday after first Monday in November; statutory odd-year grandfathering phasing out)
jurisdictions.runoffCitation: Minn. Stat. § 205.065 (Plurality election; nonpartisan primary in August held if more than twice the candidates file; Ranked-Choice Voting authorized for home rule charters, e.g. Minneapolis, St. Paul)
jurisdictions.seatStructureDefault: pure_at_large (Statutory cities: Mayor + 4 Councilmembers elected at-large with staggered 4-year terms: Minn. Stat. § 412.02)
jurisdictions.mayorSelectionNote: Direct election across all forms (2- or 4-yr term). In Statutory Plan A/B, Mayor is an ordinary member of the 5-member council with NO veto power. Strong Mayor exists only by Home Rule Charter (e.g. Minneapolis, St. Paul, Duluth).
jurisdictions.electionAdministrationCitation: Minn. Stat. § 205.07 (County Auditor conducts municipal elections concurrently with federal/state general elections)
jurisdictions.electionCostRule: Pro-rata share billed by county to city treasury under Minn. Stat. § 205.17
jurisdictions.recallCitation: Minn. Stat. Ch. 412 (Absent in general law; allowed ONLY in Home Rule Charters)
jurisdictions.recallMechanics: Statutory cities CANNOT adopt recall under Minn. Stat. Ch. 412. Available ONLY if explicitly enacted in a Home Rule Charter adopted pursuant to Minn. Const. Art. XII § 4.
jurisdictions.initiativeNotes: Statutory cities lack authority to adopt citizen initiative for ordinances. Authorized ONLY in Home Rule Charters (e.g. Minneapolis, Duluth).
jurisdictions.referendumNotes: Protest referendum against general ordinances is absent in statutory cities. Mandatory referenda apply only to issuing capital improvement bonds and adopting optional plans.

jurisdictions.homeRuleAuthority: Mo. Const. Art. VI § 19, § 19(a); RSMo Ch. 71-80
jurisdictions.ballotCitation: RSMo § 115.121 (Nonpartisan default across Missouri; 3rd class cities may opt by ordinance to conduct partisan primaries)
jurisdictions.electionTimingCitation: RSMo § 115.121 (Municipal Election Day on first Tuesday after first Monday in April annually or in odd-numbered years)
jurisdictions.runoffCitation: RSMo § 115.515 (Plurality election default; candidate with highest vote total elected; City of St. Louis uses nonpartisan approval voting with top-two runoff)
jurisdictions.seatStructureDefault: two_aldermen_per_ward (4th Class: RSMo § 79.060; 3rd Class: RSMo § 77.030; staggered 2-year terms)
jurisdictions.mayorSelectionNote: Direct election across all forms (2- or 4-yr term). Mayor presides, votes on ties, holds veto overridden by 2/3 council in 3rd Class (§ 77.270) and 4th Class (§ 79.140).
jurisdictions.electionAdministrationCitation: RSMo § 115.023 (County Clerk or Board of Election Commissioners conducts municipal April elections)
jurisdictions.electionCostRule: Proportionate share billed to municipality under RSMo § 115.063
jurisdictions.recallCitation: RSMo § 77.650 (3rd Class); Charters
jurisdictions.recallMechanics: Authorized in 3rd Class cities (RSMo § 77.650; 25% signatures) and Charter cities. STRICTLY PROHIBITED in 4th Class cities (state law provides no recall mechanism for 4th class aldermen/mayor).
jurisdictions.initiativeNotes: Authorized in 3rd Class optional forms (§ 78.200; 25% signatures) and Charter cities. PROHIBITED in 4th Class cities.
jurisdictions.referendumNotes: In 3rd Class cities, 25% voter petition filed within 10 days of passage suspends ordinance. In Charter cities, window is typically 30 days.

jurisdictions.homeRuleAuthority: Miss. Code Ann. Title 21; Miss. Const. Art. 4 § 88
jurisdictions.ballotCitation: Miss. Code § 21-11-1 et seq. (MANDATORY PARTISAN ELECTIONS: municipal primary elections conducted by municipal party executive committees)
jurisdictions.electionTimingCitation: Miss. Code § 21-11-7, § 21-11-11 (First primary on first Tuesday in April; Second primary on fourth Tuesday in April; General Election on first Tuesday after first Monday in June every 4 years, e.g. 2021, 2025, 2029)
jurisdictions.runoffCitation: Miss. Code § 23-15-305 (MANDATORY MAJORITY in party primaries: candidate must receive majority of votes; top-two runoff held 3 weeks later in April; plurality wins in June general election)
jurisdictions.seatStructureDefault: hybrid_wards_and_at_large (Code Charter cities > 10,000: 6 aldermen from wards, 1 at-large: Miss. Code § 21-3-7)
jurisdictions.mayorSelectionNote: Direct election across all forms (4-yr term). Strong Mayor under Miss. Code § 21-8-15 (Jackson: full veto overridden by 2/3 council). Weak Mayor under Code Charter (presides, votes on ties, holds suspensive veto overridden by 2/3 aldermen; § 21-3-15).
jurisdictions.electionAdministrationCitation: Miss. Code § 21-11-1 (Municipal Election Commission administers general elections; Municipal Party Executive Committees conduct party primaries)
jurisdictions.electionCostRule: 100% municipal responsibility
jurisdictions.recallCitation: Miss. Code Ann. § 25-5-1 et seq.
jurisdictions.recallMechanics: Governor appoints 3-member removal council of citizens; council investigates and verifies grounds; if certified, Governor orders special recall election. Yes/No vote; if recalled, seat is vacant.
jurisdictions.initiativeNotes: Authorized ONLY in Commission and Council-Manager forms (petition signed by 20% of qualified electors). Barred in Code Charter and Mayor-Council cities.
jurisdictions.referendumNotes: Authorized in Commission and Council-Manager forms (20% voter petition within 30 days suspends ordinance). Barred in Code Charters.

jurisdictions.homeRuleAuthority: Mont. Const. Art. XI §§ 5, 6; MCA Title 7 Ch. 3
jurisdictions.ballotCitation: MCA § 13-14-111 ('Candidates for municipal office must be nominated and elected on a nonpartisan ballot')
jurisdictions.electionTimingCitation: MCA § 13-1-104 (First Tuesday after first Monday in November of odd-numbered years)
jurisdictions.runoffCitation: MCA § 13-14-115 (Plurality election; nonpartisan primary held in September if more than twice the candidates file for a seat)
jurisdictions.seatStructureDefault: two_councilmembers_per_ward (Statutory cities: MCA § 7-3-214; staggered 4-year terms)
jurisdictions.mayorSelectionNote: Direct election in Commission-Executive (4-yr term; administrative head with veto overridden by 2/3 council; MCA § 7-3-203). Commission-Manager selects presiding mayor from commission membership.
jurisdictions.electionAdministrationCitation: MCA § 13-1-401 (County election administrator conducts municipal general and primary elections)
jurisdictions.electionCostRule: Proportionate costs billed to municipality under MCA § 13-1-402
jurisdictions.recallCitation: Mont. Const. Art. XI § 8; MCA Title 2 Ch. 16 Pt. 6 (Montana Recall Act)
jurisdictions.recallMechanics: Statutory grounds required. Officer may challenge legal sufficiency in District Court before petition circulation. 15% (cities > 1,000) or 20% (< 1,000) signatures. Standalone Yes/No recall election; vacancy filled by appointment.
jurisdictions.initiativeCitation: Mont. Const. Art. XI § 8; MCA Title 7 Ch. 5 Pt. 1 (§ 7-5-131 et seq.)
jurisdictions.initiativeNotes: 15% of registered electors. Governing body must pass ordinance without amendment within 60 days or submit to voters at next election.
jurisdictions.referendumNotes: 10% registered voter petition filed within 60 days of ordinance passage suspends ordinance pending election.

jurisdictions.homeRuleAuthority: N.C. Const. Art. VII § 1; N.C.G.S. Ch. 160A
jurisdictions.ballotCitation: N.C.G.S. § 163-291 (State law provides 4 electoral options selectable by charter: (1) Nonpartisan plurality, (2) Nonpartisan runoff, (3) Nonpartisan primary, or (4) Partisan primary and election)
jurisdictions.electionTimingCitation: N.C.G.S. § 163-279 (First Tuesday after first Monday in November of odd-numbered years; e.g. 2023, 2025, 2027)
jurisdictions.runoffCitation: N.C.G.S. § 163-293 (Under nonpartisan runoff option, majority required; runner-up may demand second election held 4 weeks later; if not demanded, leading candidate elected)
jurisdictions.seatStructureDefault: pure_at_large (small towns) / hybrid (Charlotte, Raleigh, Greensboro)
jurisdictions.mayorSelectionNote: Mayor elected at-large in ~95% of charters (2- or 4-yr term). Under Council-Manager form, Mayor is presiding council member with ceremonial duties and NO veto power (N.C.G.S. § 160A-69).
jurisdictions.electionAdministrationCitation: N.C.G.S. § 163-280 (County Board of Elections conducts all municipal elections)
jurisdictions.electionCostRule: 100% reimbursed by municipality to county board under N.C.G.S. § 163-284
jurisdictions.recallCitation: N.C.G.S. Ch. 160A (Absent in general law; exists only in ~30 local charter acts)
jurisdictions.recallMechanics: Recall is PROHIBITED under general state law. Available ONLY where enacted by the General Assembly in a specific local legislative charter act (e.g. Raleigh, Durham, Greensboro).
jurisdictions.initiativeNotes: Citizen ordinance initiative is PROHIBITED under general law; voter initiative permitted only on structural charter amendments under N.C.G.S. § 160A-104 (10% voter petition).
jurisdictions.referendumNotes: No general statutory protest referendum mechanism on municipal ordinances.

jurisdictions.homeRuleAuthority: N.D. Const. Art. VII § 6; N.D.C.C. Ch. 40-05.1 (Home Rule)
jurisdictions.ballotCitation: N.D.C.C. § 40-21-06 ('All municipal officers must be nominated and elected on nonpartisan ballots')
jurisdictions.electionTimingCitation: N.D.C.C. § 40-21-02 (Second Tuesday in June of even-numbered years, consolidated with statewide primary election)
jurisdictions.runoffCitation: N.D.C.C. § 40-21-17 (Plurality election; candidate receiving highest number of votes elected; no runoffs; Fargo uses Approval Voting)
jurisdictions.seatStructureDefault: single_member_wards (Council cities: N.D.C.C. § 40-08-01) / at-large (Commission cities: § 40-09-01)
jurisdictions.mayorSelectionNote: Direct election across all forms (4-yr term). In Council cities, Mayor presides, votes on ties, holds veto overridden by 2/3 council (§ 40-08-07). In Commission cities, President of Board of City Commissioners is executive head.
jurisdictions.electionAdministrationCitation: N.D.C.C. § 40-21-02 (County Auditor conducts municipal election in June concurrently with state primary)
jurisdictions.electionCostRule: Proportional reimbursement of costs to county under N.D.C.C. § 16.1-05-05
jurisdictions.recallCitation: N.D.C.C. § 44-08-21; N.D. Const. Art. VII § 6
jurisdictions.recallMechanics: Universal statutory recall. 25% of total votes cast for Governor in that jurisdiction in last general election. Replacement election format: incumbent automatically on ballot unless resigning.
jurisdictions.initiativeNotes: Authorized in Commission and Modern Council forms (§ 40-12-02; 15% of votes cast for executive head). Council must enact without alteration within 20 days or submit to voters.
jurisdictions.referendumNotes: 10% voter petition filed within 10 days of passage suspends ordinance until council repeals or election held.

jurisdictions.homeRuleAuthority: Neb. Const. Art. XI § 2 (Home Rule Charters); Neb. Rev. Stat. Ch. 16, 17, 18, 19
jurisdictions.ballotCitation: Neb. Rev. Stat. § 32-556 ('All municipal offices shall be nonpartisan offices')
jurisdictions.electionTimingCitation: Neb. Rev. Stat. § 32-401, § 32-556 (Primary on first Tuesday after second Monday in May; General Election on first Tuesday after first Monday in November of even-numbered years)
jurisdictions.runoffCitation: Neb. Rev. Stat. § 32-556 (Statewide nonpartisan primary in May eliminates all but top two candidates who advance to November general; plurality in November)
jurisdictions.seatStructureDefault: two_councilmembers_per_ward (1st Class cities: § 16-302; 2nd Class: § 17-102; staggered 4-year terms)
jurisdictions.mayorSelectionNote: Direct election in Mayor-Council (4-yr term; holds veto overridden by 2/3 council; § 16-303). In City Manager cities, Council elects mayor as president (§ 19-617).
jurisdictions.electionAdministrationCitation: Neb. Rev. Stat. § 32-401 et seq. (County Election Commissioner or County Clerk conducts municipal elections on statewide ballot)
jurisdictions.electionCostRule: Proportional reimbursement billed to city by county under § 32-1201
jurisdictions.recallCitation: Neb. Rev. Stat. § 32-1301 et seq. (Nebraska Recall Act)
jurisdictions.recallMechanics: Universal statutory recall. 35% of total votes cast for that office at last general election. Rapid circulation window (30 days). Standalone Yes/No ballot; if recalled, vacancy filled by appointment.
jurisdictions.initiativeCitation: Neb. Rev. Stat. § 18-2501 et seq. (Municipal Initiative and Referendum Act)
jurisdictions.initiativeNotes: 15% of registered voters. City council has 30 days to pass measure without amendment or submit to voters.
jurisdictions.referendumNotes: 15% registered voter petition filed within 30 days of passage suspends ordinance pending election.

jurisdictions.homeRuleAuthority: N.H. Const. Pt. I Art. 39; RSA Title 3 (Towns), Title 4 (Cities), RSA 49-B
jurisdictions.ballotCitation: RSA 669:1 et seq. (Town elections nonpartisan; city charters prescribe nonpartisan ballots)
jurisdictions.electionTimingCitation: RSA 669:1 (Annual town meeting on second Tuesday in March; Cities hold municipal elections on first Tuesday after first Monday in November of odd-numbered years)
jurisdictions.runoffCitation: RSA 669:54 (Plurality election; candidate receiving highest number of votes elected; no runoffs)
jurisdictions.seatStructureDefault: pure_at_large (Towns: Board of Selectmen 3 or 5 members: RSA 41:8; staggered 3-year terms)
jurisdictions.mayorSelectionNote: In towns, Selectmen elect chair. In cities, Mayor directly elected (Manchester, Nashua: strong executive authority with veto; RSA 44:11).
jurisdictions.electionAdministrationCitation: RSA 669:7 (Town/City Clerk and elected Town Moderators conduct all local elections)
jurisdictions.electionCostRule: 100% municipal responsibility
jurisdictions.recallCitation: RSA Title 3 & 4 (Absent in general law; NH Supreme Court bars recall absent statute)
jurisdictions.recallMechanics: Recall is PROHIBITED under general law. Removal of municipal officials is available only for cause via Superior Court judicial hearing under RSA 41:16-c.
jurisdictions.initiativeNotes: 25 or more registered voters petition Selectmen to include any warrant article on annual Town Meeting warrant; Selectmen have mandatory duty to insert.
jurisdictions.referendumNotes: Under SB 2, all warrant articles are voted on by secret official ballot on second Tuesday in March following a deliberative session.

jurisdictions.homeRuleAuthority: N.J. Const. Art. IV § VII par. 11; Optional Municipal Charter Law (Faulkner Act, N.J.S.A. 40:69A-1 et seq.)
jurisdictions.ballotCitation: N.J.S.A. 19:1-1 et seq. (Partisan general elections default in Boroughs/Townships; Faulkner Act permits nonpartisan option under N.J.S.A. 40:69A-161.1)
jurisdictions.electionTimingCitation: N.J.S.A. 40:69A-161.1 (Faulkner cities may hold nonpartisan elections on second Tuesday in May, or in November; Boroughs/Townships hold partisan elections in November annually)
jurisdictions.runoffCitation: N.J.S.A. 40:69A-160, 40:69A-161.1 (Faulkner nonpartisan municipalities may opt for majority runoff or pure plurality; runoff held on 4th Tuesday after election)
jurisdictions.seatStructureDefault: pure_at_large (Boroughs: 6 councilmembers elected at-large: N.J.S.A. 40A:60-2) / hybrid in Faulkner cities
jurisdictions.mayorSelectionNote: Direct election in Faulkner Mayor-Council (strong executive with veto; N.J.S.A. 40:69A-41). Weak mayor in Boroughs (presides, votes on ties, holds suspensive veto overridden by 2/3 council; N.J.S.A. 40A:60-5). In Townships, committee selects mayor.
jurisdictions.electionAdministrationCitation: N.J.S.A. Title 19 (County Board of Elections and County Clerk conduct November elections; Municipal Clerk conducts May nonpartisan elections)
jurisdictions.electionCostRule: Reimbursed to county in November; 100% municipal in May
jurisdictions.recallCitation: N.J. Const. Art. I par. 2(b); N.J.S.A. 19:27A-1 et seq. (Uniform Recall Election Law)
jurisdictions.recallMechanics: Universal constitutional right across all municipal forms. 25% of registered voters. Two-question ballot: (1) 'Shall [Officer] be recalled?' (2) Successor candidates.
jurisdictions.initiativeNotes: Authorized ONLY in Faulkner Act municipalities (10% registered voters for regular election; 15% for special election). Council must pass within 20 days or submit to voters. PROHIBITED in traditional Boroughs and Townships.
jurisdictions.referendumNotes: Authorized in Faulkner Act cities (15% registered voter petition filed within 20 days suspends ordinance until council repeals or voters approve).

jurisdictions.homeRuleAuthority: N.M. Const. Art. X § 6 (Municipal Home Rule Amendment); NMSA 1978 Ch. 3
jurisdictions.ballotCitation: NMSA 1978 § 1-22-3 (Local Election Act mandates strictly nonpartisan ballots)
jurisdictions.electionTimingCitation: NMSA 1978 § 1-22-3 (Regular Local Election held on first Tuesday after first Monday in November of odd-numbered years)
jurisdictions.runoffCitation: NMSA 1978 § 1-22-16 (Plurality default; municipality may by ordinance adopt top-two runoff requirement with 40% or 50% threshold under § 1-22-16(B))
jurisdictions.seatStructureDefault: single_member_districts (NMSA § 3-12-1; cities divided into 4 to 8 council districts; staggered 4-year terms)
jurisdictions.mayorSelectionNote: Direct election in Mayor-Council (4-yr term; holds veto overridden by 2/3 council; NMSA § 3-11-5). In Commission-Manager, Commission selects mayor as presiding officer (§ 3-14-10).
jurisdictions.electionAdministrationCitation: NMSA 1978 § 1-22-1 et seq. (Local Election Act consolidated all local elections under County Clerk)
jurisdictions.electionCostRule: State Local Election Assessment Fund pays operational costs; no direct municipal billing
jurisdictions.recallCitation: NMSA 1978 § 3-14-15 (Commission-Manager); Charters
jurisdictions.recallMechanics: Authorized in Commission-Manager cities (§ 3-14-15; 20% signatures) and Charter cities (Albuquerque: 33.3% signatures). Barred in standard Mayor-Council statutory cities.
jurisdictions.initiativeNotes: Authorized in Commission-Manager cities (20% registered voters) and Charter cities. Council must pass within 30 days or submit to election.
jurisdictions.referendumNotes: In Commission-Manager cities, 20% registered voter petition filed within 30 days suspends ordinance until voted upon.

jurisdictions.homeRuleAuthority: NRS Title 21 (NRS Ch. 266, 268); Nev. Const. Art. 15 § 3
jurisdictions.ballotCitation: NRS § 293C.110 ('All municipal elections must be nonpartisan')
jurisdictions.electionTimingCitation: NRS § 293C.110 (Preemptively consolidated all municipal elections with statewide even-year Primary in June and General in November)
jurisdictions.runoffCitation: NRS § 293C.180 (Primary in June eliminates all but top two candidates who advance to November; if a candidate in a charter city receives majority in primary, charter may declare them elected)
jurisdictions.seatStructureDefault: single_member_wards (Las Vegas: 6 wards; Reno: 6 wards; Henderson: 4 wards)
jurisdictions.mayorSelectionNote: Direct election across all cities (4-yr term). 12-YEAR LIFETIME TERM LIMIT applies to all municipal elected officials under Nev. Const. Art. 15 § 3. Council-Manager form dominates; mayor is council member/presiding officer with ceremonial headship.
jurisdictions.electionAdministrationCitation: NRS § 293C.110 (County Registrar of Voters / County Clerk conducts municipal elections)
jurisdictions.electionCostRule: Pro-rata reimbursement of direct costs to county
jurisdictions.recallCitation: Nev. Const. Art. 2 § 9; NRS Ch. 306
jurisdictions.recallMechanics: Universal constitutional right. 25% of voters who actually voted in the election at which the officer was elected. Two-question ballot: (1) 'Shall [Officer] be recalled?' (2) Successor ballot.
jurisdictions.initiativeCitation: Nev. Const. Art. 19 § 4; NRS § 295.205 et seq.
jurisdictions.initiativeNotes: 15% of registered voters. Council has 30 days to enact ordinance without change or submit to voters at next general election.
jurisdictions.referendumNotes: 10% of registered voters filed within 30 days suspends ordinance until council repeals or voters ratify.

jurisdictions.homeRuleAuthority: N.Y. Const. Art. IX (Home Rule); Municipal Home Rule Law (MHRL); Town Law; Village Law
jurisdictions.ballotCitation: N.Y. Election Law § 6-108, § 6-110 (MANDATORY PARTISAN ELECTIONS: party nominations via June primary or town caucus; independent nominating petitions)
jurisdictions.electionTimingCitation: N.Y. Election Law § 8-100 (Primary in June; General Election on first Tuesday after first Monday in November of odd-numbered years; independent villages hold March/June elections)
jurisdictions.runoffCitation: N.Y. Election Law § 9-212 (Plurality election; candidate with highest vote total elected; NYC uses Ranked-Choice Voting in primaries only under City Charter § 1057-g)
jurisdictions.seatStructureDefault: pure_at_large (Towns & Villages) / single_member_districts (Cities per individual charters)
jurisdictions.seatStructureCitation: Town Law § 20, Village Law § 3-301, Local City Charters
jurisdictions.mayorSelectionNote: Direct popular election across all cities and villages (2- or 4-yr term). Strong Mayor in major cities (NYC, Buffalo, Syracuse, Albany: executive appointments, veto overridden by 2/3 council). In towns, Supervisor is presiding town board member.
jurisdictions.electionAdministrationCitation: N.Y. Election Law § 3-200 et seq. (Bipartisan County Board of Elections conducts all general, primary, and town elections; villages may conduct independent March elections)
jurisdictions.electionCostRule: Apportioned and charged back to municipality under N.Y. Elec. Law § 4-136
jurisdictions.vacancyCitation: Public Officers Law § 42; Town Law § 64(5); Village Law § 3-312
jurisdictions.recallCitation: Matter of Cassella v. City of Schenectady, 281 A.D. 428 (1953); Public Officers Law § 36
jurisdictions.recallMechanics: MUNICIPAL RECALL IS UNCONSTITUTIONAL IN NEW YORK. Appellate Division ruled that local recall charters violate state public officers law and constitution. Removal available ONLY via judicial proceeding in Appellate Division for malfeasance under Public Officers Law § 36.
jurisdictions.initiativeNotes: Citizen initiative for ordinary municipal ordinances is PROHIBITED. Voter initiative permitted ONLY for proposing amendments to a city charter (petition signed by 30,000 electors or 10% of votes cast for Governor under MHRL § 37).
jurisdictions.referendumNotes: No general protest referendum on ordinary ordinances. Permissive referendum (protest petition) applies ONLY to structural local laws enumerated in MHRL § 24 (e.g. changing term of office, reducing council salary, curtailing powers of elected official).

jurisdictions.homeRuleAuthority: Ohio Const. Art. XVIII §§ 3, 7 (1912 Home Rule Amendment); R.C. Title 7
jurisdictions.ballotCitation: R.C. § 3513.01, § 3505.04 (MANDATORY PARTISAN ELECTIONS in statutory cities: candidates run in party primaries in May; Charter cities universally prescribe nonpartisan ballots under Art. XVIII § 3)
jurisdictions.electionTimingCitation: R.C. § 3501.01, § 3501.02 (Primary on first Tuesday after first Monday in May; General Election on first Tuesday after first Monday in November of odd-numbered years)
jurisdictions.runoffCitation: R.C. § 3505.33 (Plurality election; candidate with highest vote total elected; no general election runoffs)
jurisdictions.seatStructureDefault: hybrid_wards_and_at_large (Statutory cities: 7 councilmembers: 4 ward, 3 at-large: R.C. § 731.01; 2-year terms)
jurisdictions.mayorSelectionNote: Direct election in statutory cities (4-yr term; full executive administration, veto overridden by 2/3 council; R.C. § 731.27, § 733.01). In statutory villages, Mayor presides, votes on ties, holds veto. Charter cities establish strong mayor (Cleveland, Columbus, Cincinnati) or council-manager (Dayton).
jurisdictions.electionAdministrationCitation: R.C. § 3501.11 (Bipartisan County Board of Elections conducts all municipal elections)
jurisdictions.electionCostRule: Proportionate share billed by county to municipal treasury under R.C. § 3501.17
jurisdictions.recallCitation: Ohio Const. Art. II § 1f; R.C. Ch. 705; Charters
jurisdictions.recallMechanics: Statutory cities under Title 7 lack recall; universally adopted in Charter cities pursuant to Home Rule Amendment (typically 15-25% signatures).
jurisdictions.initiativeNotes: UNIVERSAL CONSTITUTIONAL RIGHT. 10% of electors who voted for Governor at last election. Petition filed with city auditor; auditor certifies to board of elections after 10 days.
jurisdictions.referendumNotes: UNIVERSAL CONSTITUTIONAL RIGHT. 10% voter petition filed within 30 days of ordinance passage SUSPENDS ordinance until approved at next general election.

jurisdictions.homeRuleAuthority: Okla. Const. Art. XVIII § 3(a); 11 O.S. § 1-101 et seq. (Oklahoma Municipal Code)
jurisdictions.ballotCitation: 11 O.S. § 16-101 et seq. (Nonpartisan default; political party committee may petition for partisan primary: 11 O.S. § 16-106)
jurisdictions.electionTimingCitation: 11 O.S. § 16-101 (Primary on second Tuesday in February; General Election on first Tuesday in April of odd-numbered years; cities may adopt resolution to hold elections in even-numbered years)
jurisdictions.runoffCitation: 11 O.S. § 16-103 (Candidate receiving majority of votes cast at February primary is elected; if no candidate clears 50%, top two advance to April general)
jurisdictions.seatStructureDefault: two_aldermen_per_ward (Aldermanic: 11 O.S. § 9-102) / single-member wards (Manager: 11 O.S. § 10-102)
jurisdictions.mayorSelectionNote: Direct election in Aldermanic and Strong-Mayor (4-yr term; holds veto in Strong-Mayor: 11 O.S. § 11-108). In Council-Manager, Council selects Mayor from its membership as presiding chair (§ 10-105).
jurisdictions.electionAdministrationCitation: 11 O.S. § 16-105; 26 O.S. § 13-101 (County Election Board conducts all municipal elections on state voting machines)
jurisdictions.electionCostRule: Reimbursed by municipality to County Election Board under 26 O.S. § 13-111
jurisdictions.recallCitation: Okla. Const. Art. VIII § 8; Charters
jurisdictions.recallMechanics: Charter cities universally provide recall (typically 20-30% signatures). Absent in statutory general plans.
jurisdictions.initiativeCitation: Okla. Const. Art. XVIII § 4(a); 11 O.S. § 15-101 et seq.
jurisdictions.initiativeNotes: UNIVERSAL CONSTITUTIONAL RIGHT. 25% of total votes cast at last general municipal election. Council has 30 days to enact or call election.
jurisdictions.referendumNotes: UNIVERSAL CONSTITUTIONAL RIGHT. 25% voter petition filed within 30 days of publication suspends ordinance pending election.

jurisdictions.homeRuleAuthority: Or. Const. Art. XI § 2 (1906 Municipal Home Rule Amendment); ORS Ch. 221
jurisdictions.ballotCitation: ORS § 249.002, § 254.005 ('All municipal elections shall be nonpartisan')
jurisdictions.electionTimingCitation: ORS § 221.230, § 254.056 (Primary on third Tuesday in May; General Election on first Tuesday after first Monday in November of even-numbered years; all mail-ballot)
jurisdictions.runoffCitation: ORS § 249.088 (Candidate receiving majority of votes in May primary is elected outright; otherwise, top two candidates advance to November general)
jurisdictions.seatStructureDefault: pure_at_large (majority of charters) / multi-member districts (Portland: 3 members per district using Single Transferable Vote)
jurisdictions.mayorSelectionNote: Direct election across nearly all charters (2- or 4-yr term). Weak/presiding mayor in Council-Manager cities (Eugene, Salem). Portland 2024 reform created executive Mayor with professional City Administrator.
jurisdictions.electionAdministrationCitation: ORS § 254.005 et seq. (County Clerk conducts all municipal elections under Oregon's 100% Vote-by-Mail system)
jurisdictions.electionCostRule: Pro-rata share billed by county to city under ORS § 254.046
jurisdictions.recallCitation: Or. Const. Art. II § 18; ORS Ch. 249
jurisdictions.recallMechanics: Universal constitutional right. 15% of total votes cast for Governor in that jurisdiction. Official has 5 days to resign; if not, special recall election ordered within 35 days. Yes/No recall question + successor candidates.
jurisdictions.initiativeCitation: Or. Const. Art. IV § 1(5); ORS § 250.255 et seq.
jurisdictions.initiativeNotes: UNIVERSAL CONSTITUTIONAL RIGHT. 15% of total votes cast for Governor. Council has 30 days to enact without change or submit to voters.
jurisdictions.referendumNotes: UNIVERSAL CONSTITUTIONAL RIGHT. 10% voter petition filed within 30 days of ordinance adoption suspends ordinance pending election.

jurisdictions.homeRuleAuthority: Pa. Const. Art. IX § 2; Home Rule Charter and Optional Plans Law (53 Pa.C.S. § 2901 et seq.)
jurisdictions.ballotCitation: 25 P.S. § 2862 et seq. (MANDATORY PARTISAN ELECTIONS: party primaries in May; general election in November of odd-numbered years)
jurisdictions.electionTimingCitation: Pa. Const. Art. VII § 3; 25 P.S. § 2754 (Municipal Primary on third Tuesday in May; Municipal Election on first Tuesday after first Monday in November of odd-numbered years)
jurisdictions.runoffCitation: 25 P.S. § 3156 (Plurality election; candidate with highest vote total elected; no runoffs)
jurisdictions.seatStructureDefault: pure_at_large (Boroughs & 3rd Class cities) / wards (Pittsburgh, Philadelphia)
jurisdictions.mayorSelectionNote: Direct election across all forms (4-yr term). In Boroughs, Mayor is weak (presides over police department, votes on council ties, holds suspensive veto overridden by 2/3 council; 8 Pa.C.S. § 1007). Strong Mayor exists in 1st/2nd Class cities (Philly, Pittsburgh) and Home Rule charters.
jurisdictions.electionAdministrationCitation: 25 P.S. § 2641 et seq. (County Board of Elections conducts all municipal elections)
jurisdictions.electionCostRule: 100% borne by county treasury (no municipal chargeback for general elections)
jurisdictions.recallCitation: Pa. Const. Art. VI § 7; Citizens Committee to Recall Rizzo v. Board of Elections, 470 Pa. 1 (1976)
jurisdictions.recallMechanics: MUNICIPAL RECALL IS UNCONSTITUTIONAL IN PENNSYLVANIA. The Supreme Court of Pennsylvania held in Citizens Committee to Recall Rizzo (1976) that Article VI Section 7 of the Pennsylvania Constitution establishes the EXCLUSIVE methods for removing elected officers (impeachment or judicial conviction of misbehavior), and local recall charters violate the constitution.
jurisdictions.initiativeNotes: Citizen initiative for general municipal ordinances is ABSENT under standard statutory codes. Available ONLY if explicitly enacted in a Home Rule Charter adopted pursuant to 53 Pa.C.S. § 2971.
jurisdictions.referendumNotes: General protest referendum on municipal ordinances does not exist in standard statutory codes. Home Rule charters may authorize protest referenda.

jurisdictions.homeRuleAuthority: R.I. Const. Art. XIII (Home Rule); R.I. Gen. Laws Title 45
jurisdictions.ballotCitation: R.I.G.L. Title 17 (Partisan in cities like Providence and Cranston; nonpartisan in towns like Newport and South Kingstown per charter)
jurisdictions.electionTimingCitation: R.I.G.L. § 17-1-2, § 17-18-1 (Primary in September; General Election on first Tuesday after first Monday in November of even-numbered years)
jurisdictions.runoffCitation: R.I.G.L. § 17-19-36 (Plurality election; candidate with highest vote total elected; no runoffs)
jurisdictions.seatStructureDefault: pure_at_large (Town Councils 5 or 7 members: R.I.G.L. § 45-4-1) / wards in cities
jurisdictions.mayorSelectionNote: Direct election in Mayor-Council charters (Providence, Warwick: strong executive administration, veto power). In towns, Town Council selects Council President as presiding officer.
jurisdictions.electionAdministrationCitation: R.I.G.L. § 17-7-1 et seq. (Local Board of Canvassers in each city/town administers elections under supervision of State Board of Elections)
jurisdictions.electionCostRule: State Board provides voting equipment; local canvassing board costs borne by municipality
jurisdictions.recallCitation: Charters pursuant to R.I. Const. Art. XIII
jurisdictions.recallMechanics: Authorized ONLY where explicitly enacted in a municipal Home Rule Charter (e.g. Cranston, Warwick). Absent under general state law.
jurisdictions.initiativeNotes: Direct democracy exercised via Financial Town Meeting (FTM) where voters directly approve municipal budget and tax levies. In cities, initiative exists only where granted by charter.
jurisdictions.referendumNotes: Governed by municipal charters; protest petitions suspend ordinances where charter provides.

jurisdictions.homeRuleAuthority: S.C. Const. Art. VIII; Home Rule Act of 1975 (S.C. Code Ann. Title 5)
jurisdictions.ballotCitation: S.C. Code Ann. § 5-15-60 (Municipality must determine by ordinance: (1) Nonpartisan plurality, (2) Nonpartisan runoff, or (3) Partisan primary and general election)
jurisdictions.electionTimingCitation: S.C. Code Ann. § 5-15-50 (Municipality fixes election dates by ordinance; commonly first Tuesday after first Monday in November of odd-numbered years, or spring dates)
jurisdictions.runoffCitation: S.C. Code Ann. § 5-15-61, § 5-15-62 (If nonpartisan runoff option adopted, candidate must receive majority of votes; otherwise top two advance to runoff held 2 weeks later)
jurisdictions.seatStructureDefault: pure_at_large (small towns) / single_member_districts (Columbia, Charleston)
jurisdictions.mayorSelectionNote: Direct election across all forms (2- or 4-yr term). Strong Mayor under § 5-9-30 (Charleston, Columbia: full administrative appointment, veto overridden by 2/3 council). In Council and Manager forms, Mayor has no veto.
jurisdictions.electionAdministrationCitation: S.C. Code Ann. § 5-15-145 (Municipalities may transfer election administration to County Board of Voter Registration and Elections)
jurisdictions.electionCostRule: Municipality reimburses County Board for actual election expenses
jurisdictions.recallCitation: S.C. Code Ann. Title 5; Op. S.C. Att'y Gen. (July 19, 2007)
jurisdictions.recallMechanics: MUNICIPAL RECALL IS PROHIBITED in South Carolina. State statutes provide no recall authority for municipal officers. Removal is available only via Governor under S.C. Const. Art. VI § 8 for indictment of crimes involving moral turpitude.
jurisdictions.initiativeNotes: UNIVERSAL STATUTORY RIGHT. Petition signed by 15% of registered electors. Council must pass ordinance without amendment within 60 days or submit to election.
jurisdictions.referendumNotes: UNIVERSAL STATUTORY RIGHT. 15% registered elector petition filed within 60 days suspends ordinance until council repeals or election held.

jurisdictions.homeRuleAuthority: S.D. Const. Art. IX § 2; SDCL Ch. 9-14A (Home Rule)
jurisdictions.ballotCitation: SDCL § 9-13-6 ('All municipal elections shall be nonpartisan')
jurisdictions.electionTimingCitation: SDCL § 9-13-1 (Second Tuesday in April annually; municipalities may choose to hold election on first Tuesday after first Monday in June consolidated with statewide primary)
jurisdictions.runoffCitation: SDCL § 9-13-26, § 9-13-27 (Secondary election required if no candidate receives majority, unless municipality adopts plurality ordinance under § 9-13-27.1)
jurisdictions.seatStructureDefault: two_aldermen_per_ward (Aldermanic: SDCL § 9-8-1; staggered terms)
jurisdictions.mayorSelectionNote: Direct election across all forms (2- or 4-yr term). Mayor presides, votes on ties, holds veto overridden by 2/3 council in Aldermanic form (SDCL § 9-8-3).
jurisdictions.electionAdministrationCitation: SDCL Ch. 9-13 (Finance Officer conducts standalone municipal elections; County Auditor conducts if consolidated with June primary)
jurisdictions.electionCostRule: 100% municipal in April; shared in June
jurisdictions.recallCitation: SDCL § 9-13-29 et seq.
jurisdictions.recallMechanics: Universal statutory recall. Petition signed by 15% of registered voters. Incumbent is automatically a candidate on the recall ballot unless declining; challengers run alongside; plurality winner takes office.
jurisdictions.initiativeCitation: S.D. Const. Art. III § 1; SDCL Ch. 9-20
jurisdictions.initiativeNotes: FIRST STATE IN THE NATION to adopt initiative (1898). Petition signed by 5% of registered voters. Submitted to voters at next annual municipal election or special election.
jurisdictions.referendumNotes: Petition signed by 5% of registered voters filed within 20 days after ordinance publication suspends ordinance pending election.

jurisdictions.homeRuleAuthority: Tenn. Const. Art. XI § 9 (Home Rule Amendment of 1953); T.C.A. Title 6
jurisdictions.ballotCitation: T.C.A. § 2-13-208 (Nonpartisan default; private act charters may authorize partisan elections)
jurisdictions.electionTimingCitation: T.C.A. § 6-53-101; County Election Commission (Municipal elections commonly held in August or November of even-numbered years, or standalone May/September per charter)
jurisdictions.runoffCitation: T.C.A. § 2-8-110 (Plurality election; candidate with highest vote total elected; Metropolitan Nashville requires 50%+1 with runoff under Charter § 15.01)
jurisdictions.seatStructureDefault: pure_at_large (Commission charters) / wards (Mayor-Aldermanic: T.C.A. § 6-1-201)
jurisdictions.mayorSelectionNote: Direct election in Mayor-Aldermanic (T.C.A. § 6-3-101; administrative head, veto power overridden by 2/3 board). In Manager-Commission, Commission elects mayor from membership as ceremonial head (§ 6-20-201).
jurisdictions.electionAdministrationCitation: T.C.A. § 2-12-116 (County Election Commission conducts all municipal elections on county voting machines)
jurisdictions.electionCostRule: Municipality reimburses County Election Commission for actual expenses under T.C.A. § 2-12-109
jurisdictions.recallCitation: T.C.A. § 6-20-220 (Manager-Commission); Metro Charters
jurisdictions.recallMechanics: Authorized in City Manager-Commission charters (§ 6-20-220; requires 33.3% registered voters) and Metro charters (Nashville: 15% registered voters). ABSENT in general Mayor-Aldermanic charters.
jurisdictions.initiativeNotes: Authorized in Manager-Commission charters (25% voter petition). Council must pass within 60 days or submit to election. Absent in Mayor-Aldermanic cities.
jurisdictions.referendumNotes: Authorized in Manager-Commission charters (25% voter petition within 30 days suspends ordinance). Absent in Mayor-Aldermanic charters.

jurisdictions.homeRuleAuthority: Tex. Const. Art. XI § 5 (Home Rule Amendment); Tex. Loc. Gov't Code (TLGC) Title 2
jurisdictions.ballotCitation: Tex. Elec. Code § 143.002 et seq. ('Independent Candidates for Municipal Office; party labels prohibited on municipal ballots')
jurisdictions.electionTimingCitation: Tex. Elec. Code § 41.001 (Uniform Election Date on first Saturday in May annually; Home Rule charters may opt for first Tuesday after first Monday in November)
jurisdictions.runoffCitation: TLGC § 22.010; Tex. Elec. Code § 2.021 (MANDATORY MAJORITY RULE in Type A cities: candidate must receive 50%+1 of votes cast; otherwise top-two runoff held; council may adopt plurality ordinance under § 2.022)
jurisdictions.seatStructureDefault: pure_at_large (Type A: TLGC § 22.031) / single-member districts (Home Rule cities)
jurisdictions.mayorSelectionNote: Direct election across all forms (2-yr default; 3- or 4-yr terms trigger constitutional resign-to-run). In Type A, Mayor presides, votes only on ties, holds veto overridden by 2/3 aldermen (TLGC § 22.042, § 22.032). Strong Mayor in Houston; Council-Manager dominant in Dallas, Austin, San Antonio, Fort Worth, El Paso.
jurisdictions.electionAdministrationCitation: Tex. Elec. Code § 31.092 (City Secretary conducts May standalone elections, or contracts with County Elections Administrator for joint election under Ch. 271)
jurisdictions.electionCostRule: 100% municipal in May; shared cost under joint election contract
jurisdictions.recallCitation: Tex. Const. Art. XI § 5; Local Home Rule Charters
jurisdictions.recallMechanics: General Law cities (Type A, B, C) lack statutory authority for recall. UNIVERSALLY ADOPTED in Texas Home Rule Charters (typically 10-25% registered voter signatures). Two-question ballot or replacement ballot per charter.
jurisdictions.initiativeNotes: Absent in General Law cities. Universally provided in Home Rule Charters. Council must pass without amendment or submit to voters.
jurisdictions.referendumNotes: Home Rule charters grant protest referendum suspending ordinances pending vote.

jurisdictions.homeRuleAuthority: Utah Const. Art. XI § 5; Utah Code Ann. (UCA) Title 10
jurisdictions.ballotCitation: UCA § 20A-9-404 ('Municipal elections shall be nonpartisan')
jurisdictions.electionTimingCitation: UCA § 20A-1-201.5, § 20A-1-202 (Municipal Primary on second Tuesday in August; Municipal General Election on first Tuesday after first Monday in November of odd-numbered years; 100% Vote-by-Mail)
jurisdictions.runoffCitation: UCA § 20A-1-304 (Plurality election; Municipal Alternative Voting Methods Pilot Project authorizes municipalities to adopt Ranked-Choice Voting / Instant Runoff Voting under UCA § 20A-4-601 et seq.)
jurisdictions.seatStructureDefault: pure_at_large (5-member council statutory default: UCA § 10-3b-301; staggered 4-year terms) / districts in Salt Lake City
jurisdictions.mayorSelectionNote: Direct election across all forms (4-yr term). Weak Mayor in 5/6-member council: mayor presides, votes ONLY in case of a tie, and has NO veto power (UCA § 10-3b-304). Strong Mayor under § 10-3b-202: executive head with veto overridden by 2/3 council.
jurisdictions.electionAdministrationCitation: UCA § 20A-5-400.1 (Municipalities contract with County Clerk to administer mail-ballot elections)
jurisdictions.electionCostRule: Reimbursed by municipality to county under interlocal agreement
jurisdictions.recallCitation: Utah Code Title 10 & 20A; Op. Utah Att'y Gen. (1987)
jurisdictions.recallMechanics: MUNICIPAL RECALL IS PROHIBITED in Utah. The Utah Constitution and statutes provide no recall mechanism for local elected officials. Removal is available only for cause via judicial trial under UCA § 77-6-1.
jurisdictions.initiativeCitation: Utah Const. Art. VI § 1(2); UCA Title 20A Ch. 7 Pt. 5 (§ 20A-7-501 et seq.)
jurisdictions.initiativeNotes: UNIVERSAL STATUTORY RIGHT. Tiered signature thresholds: 8% (cities > 100k), 11.5% (cities 10k-100k), 16% (cities < 10k) of total votes cast for Governor in that city. Placed directly on municipal general election ballot.
jurisdictions.referendumCitation: Utah Const. Art. VI § 1(2); UCA Title 20A Ch. 7 Pt. 6 (§ 20A-7-601 et seq.)
jurisdictions.referendumNotes: Petition filed within 45 days. Does NOT automatically suspend ordinance unless court injunction issued. Voted on at next general election.

jurisdictions.homeRuleAuthority: Va. Const. Art. VII; Va. Code Title 15.2 (Counties, Cities and Towns)
jurisdictions.ballotCitation: Va. Code § 24.2-500 et seq. (Candidates run as independents or party-endorsed; no formal partisan municipal primary under general law)
jurisdictions.electionTimingCitation: Va. Code § 24.2-222.1 (HISTORIC 2021 STATUTE: Abolished historical May municipal elections; mandated all city and town council elections moved to first Tuesday after first Monday in November)
jurisdictions.runoffCitation: Va. Code § 24.2-673 (Plurality election; candidate receiving highest number of votes elected; City of Richmond requires winning a plurality in 5 of 9 council districts under Charter § 5.01)
jurisdictions.seatStructureDefault: pure_at_large (towns and smaller cities) / single_member_districts (Richmond, Norfolk, Portsmouth)
jurisdictions.seatStructureCitation: Governed by individual legislative city charters
jurisdictions.mayorSelectionNote: Direct election in Richmond (Strong Mayor with full administrative control and veto; Charter Ch. 5). In Council-Manager cities (Alexandria, Norfolk, Roanoke), Mayor is chosen by council or directly elected as ceremonial chair with NO veto power.
jurisdictions.electionAdministrationCitation: Va. Code § 24.2-109 et seq. (City or County Electoral Board and General Registrar conduct all elections on state-certified voting systems)
jurisdictions.electionCostRule: Independent cities bear 100% of their city electoral board costs
jurisdictions.recallCitation: Va. Code § 24.2-233 et seq. (Judicial Removal Trial)
jurisdictions.recallMechanics: POLITICAL RECALL DOES NOT EXIST IN VIRGINIA. Citizen petition signed by 10% of qualified voters who voted at last election acts ONLY as an application to the Circuit Court to initiate a judicial trial for removal for cause before a circuit judge.
jurisdictions.initiativeNotes: Citizen initiative for general municipal ordinances is PROHIBITED under Virginia law.
jurisdictions.referendumNotes: No general protest referendum on municipal ordinances. Advisory referenda permitted only upon circuit court order under Va. Code § 24.2-684.

jurisdictions.homeRuleAuthority: Vt. Const. Ch. II § 69; 24 V.S.A. (Municipal and County Government)
jurisdictions.ballotCitation: 17 V.S.A. § 2640 et seq. (Town elections nonpartisan; Australian ballot or floor voting)
jurisdictions.electionTimingCitation: 17 V.S.A. § 2640 (TOWN MEETING DAY: First Tuesday in March annually across the entire state)
jurisdictions.runoffCitation: 17 V.S.A. § 2660 (Plurality election; candidate receiving highest number of votes elected; City of Burlington uses Ranked-Choice Voting under Charter Sec. 5)
jurisdictions.seatStructureDefault: pure_at_large (Selectboard 3 or 5 members: 24 V.S.A. § 871; staggered 3-year terms)
jurisdictions.mayorSelectionNote: In towns, Selectboard chooses its own Chair annually (24 V.S.A. § 872). In cities, Mayor directly elected (Burlington: strong mayor with veto overridden by 2/3 council).
jurisdictions.electionAdministrationCitation: 17 V.S.A. § 2640 et seq. (Town Clerk and Board of Civil Authority conduct all Town Meeting elections)
jurisdictions.electionCostRule: 100% town responsibility
jurisdictions.recallCitation: 24 V.S.A. (Absent in general law; exists only in specific legislative charters)
jurisdictions.recallMechanics: Recall does NOT exist under general Vermont law. Available ONLY if enacted into a municipal charter by special act of the General Assembly.
jurisdictions.initiativeNotes: Petition signed by 5% of registered voters MANDATES Selectboard to insert proposed article into the warning for the annual Town Meeting.
jurisdictions.referendumNotes: Petition signed by 5% of registered voters filed within 30 days of town meeting vote forces a vote on RECONSIDERATION or RESCISSION of the measure.

jurisdictions.homeRuleAuthority: Wash. Const. Art. XI § 10; RCW Title 35 (Cities) & Title 35A (Optional Municipal Code)
jurisdictions.ballotCitation: RCW § 29A.52.210 ('All city, town, and school district offices shall be nonpartisan')
jurisdictions.electionTimingCitation: RCW § 29A.04.321, § 29A.04.330 (Top-two Primary on first Tuesday in August; General Election on first Tuesday after first Monday in November of odd-numbered years; 100% Vote-by-Mail)
jurisdictions.runoffCitation: RCW § 29A.52.210, § 29A.52.220 (Top-two primary in August eliminates all but top two candidates who advance to November general election; plurality wins in November)
jurisdictions.seatStructureDefault: pure_at_large (Code cities: RCW 35A.12.010; 5 or 7 councilmembers with staggered 4-year terms) / districts (Seattle: 7 districts, 2 at-large)
jurisdictions.seatStructureCitation: RCW 35A.12.010; Washington Voting Rights Act (RCW Ch. 29A.92)
jurisdictions.mayorSelectionNote: Direct election in Mayor-Council (4-yr term; chief executive administrator with veto overridden by majority plus one of council: RCW 35A.12.100, 35A.12.130). In Council-Manager, Council selects Mayor from own members as ceremonial chair (RCW 35A.13.030).
jurisdictions.electionAdministrationCitation: RCW § 29A.04.216 (County Auditor conducts all municipal elections under Washington's universal Vote-by-Mail system)
jurisdictions.electionCostRule: Proportional share of election costs billed by county to municipality under RCW § 29A.04.410
jurisdictions.recallCitation: Wash. Const. Art. I §§ 33, 34; RCW Title 29A Ch. 56 (§ 29A.56.110 et seq.)
jurisdictions.recallMechanics: MANDATORY JUDICIAL SUFFICIENCY HEARING: Petition cannot be circulated until a Superior Court judge conducts a formal hearing to determine whether charges are factually and legally sufficient! 25% (cities 1st/2nd class) or 35% (other cities) of votes cast for that office. Standalone Yes/No vote; vacancy filled by appointment.
jurisdictions.initiativeNotes: Authorized in Code Cities and First Class Charters (15% registered voters for regular election; 20% for special election). Council must pass within 30 days or submit to voters.
jurisdictions.referendumNotes: 10% registered voter petition filed within 30 days of ordinance passage suspends ordinance pending election.

jurisdictions.homeRuleAuthority: Wis. Const. Art. XI § 3 (Home Rule Amendment); Wis. Stat. Ch. 62 (Cities) & Ch. 61 (Villages)
jurisdictions.ballotCitation: Wis. Stat. § 5.60 ('The official spring ballot shall be nonpartisan and shall contain no party designations')
jurisdictions.electionTimingCitation: Wis. Stat. § 5.02, § 5.60 (Spring Primary on third Tuesday in February; Spring Election on first Tuesday in April annually)
jurisdictions.runoffCitation: Wis. Stat. § 5.01(4) (Plurality election; candidate receiving highest number of votes elected; nonpartisan spring primary in February eliminates all but top two candidates if > 2 file)
jurisdictions.seatStructureDefault: single_member_aldermanic_districts (Cities: Wis. Stat. § 62.08; staggered 2-year terms) / at-large (Villages: 6 Trustees: § 61.20)
jurisdictions.mayorSelectionNote: Direct election across all forms (2- or 4-yr term). Mayor is chief executive; votes on ties; holds veto over ordinances and partial/line-item veto over budget appropriations (overridden by 2/3 council: Wis. Stat. § 62.09(8)(c)). In villages, Village President presides, votes as trustee, holds no veto.
jurisdictions.electionAdministrationCitation: Wis. Stat. § 7.15 (Municipal Clerk conducts all municipal elections and maintains local voter rolls under statewide WisVote system)
jurisdictions.electionCostRule: 100% municipal responsibility
jurisdictions.recallCitation: Wis. Const. Art. XIII § 12; Wis. Stat. § 9.10
jurisdictions.recallMechanics: Universal constitutional right. 25% of total votes cast for Governor in that jurisdiction. SIMULTANEOUS REPLACEMENT BALLOT: Incumbent is automatically on recall ballot as candidate unless resigning within 10 days. Challengers file nomination papers. Plurality winner takes office.
jurisdictions.initiativeNotes: UNIVERSAL STATUTORY RIGHT. Petition signed by 15% of votes cast for Governor in municipality. Council must pass without alteration within 30 days or submit to voters at next spring or general election. Under Landt v. City of Wisconsin Dells (1966), direct legislation CANNOT be used to repeal existing legislation.
jurisdictions.referendumNotes: Protest referendum guaranteed against CHARTER ORDINANCES (petition signed by 7% of votes cast for Governor within 60 days forces referendum under Wis. Stat. § 66.0101(8)). Ordinary ordinances are subject to indirect initiative, not protest referendum.

jurisdictions.homeRuleAuthority: W. Va. Const. Art. VI § 39(a); W. Va. Code Ch. 8 (Municipal Code); § 8-1-5a (Municipal Home Rule Program)
jurisdictions.ballotCitation: W. Va. Code § 8-5-5 (Municipality determines by charter or ordinance whether elections are partisan or nonpartisan)
jurisdictions.electionTimingCitation: W. Va. Code § 8-5-5 (Election dates set by charter; commonly second Tuesday in June, or consolidated with statewide May primary of even-numbered years)
jurisdictions.runoffCitation: W. Va. Code § 8-5-11 (Plurality election; candidate with highest vote total elected; no runoffs)
jurisdictions.seatStructureDefault: pure_at_large (smaller towns) / wards (Charleston, Huntington, Wheeling)
jurisdictions.mayorSelectionNote: Direct election in Plans I, II, and IV (2- or 4-yr term). Strong Mayor under Plan II (full administrative powers, veto overridden by 2/3 council; § 8-3-3). In Plan V, council selects mayor from own membership.
jurisdictions.electionAdministrationCitation: W. Va. Code § 8-5-13 (City Recorder/Clerk conducts standalone municipal elections; County Clerk conducts if consolidated with state primary)
jurisdictions.electionCostRule: 100% municipal if standalone; proportional share if consolidated
jurisdictions.recallCitation: W. Va. Code § 8-12-4 (Recall absent in general law; allowed ONLY where explicitly provided in charter)
jurisdictions.recallMechanics: Recall is absent under general state law. Available only if explicitly enacted in a municipal charter under W. Va. Code § 8-12-4(2).
jurisdictions.initiativeNotes: Citizen initiative for ordinary municipal ordinances is not authorized by general state statute; exists only where enacted by local charter.
jurisdictions.referendumCitation: W. Va. Code § 8-1-5a (Home Rule Referendum); Charters
jurisdictions.referendumNotes: Under Municipal Home Rule statute (§ 8-1-5a), 15% voter petition filed within 30 days against any proposed home-rule ordinance forces referendum vote.

jurisdictions.homeRuleAuthority: Wyo. Const. Art. 13 § 1 (Home Rule Amendment); Wyo. Stat. Title 15
jurisdictions.ballotCitation: Wyo. Stat. § 22-23-103 ('All municipal elections shall be nonpartisan')
jurisdictions.electionTimingCitation: Wyo. Stat. § 22-23-102 (Primary on first Tuesday after third Monday in August; General Election on first Tuesday after first Monday in November of even-numbered years)
jurisdictions.runoffCitation: Wyo. Stat. § 22-23-103, § 22-23-401 (Primary in August eliminates all but top two candidates who advance to November general; plurality in November)
jurisdictions.seatStructureDefault: two_councilmen_per_ward (1st Class cities: Wyo. Stat. § 15-3-101; staggered 4-year terms) / at-large (Towns: § 15-2-101)
jurisdictions.mayorSelectionNote: Direct election in Mayor-Council (4-yr term; votes on ties, holds veto overridden by 2/3 council; § 15-3-102). In Council-Manager cities (Casper, Laramie), Council elects Mayor from own members as president (§ 15-4-102).
jurisdictions.electionAdministrationCitation: Wyo. Stat. § 22-23-102 (County Clerk conducts all municipal elections concurrently with county/state elections)
jurisdictions.electionCostRule: Proportionate share billed by county to city under Wyo. Stat. § 22-23-104
jurisdictions.recallCitation: Wyo. Stat. § 15-1-1101 et seq.
jurisdictions.recallMechanics: Universal statutory recall across all cities and towns. 25% of total votes cast for that office at last general election. Two-question ballot: (1) 'Shall [Officer] be recalled?' (2) Successor candidates. If recalled, successor takes office.
jurisdictions.initiativeNotes: Authorized in Commission and City Manager forms (20-25% of registered electors). Council must pass within 20 days or submit to voters. Limited in Mayor-Council cities.
jurisdictions.referendumNotes: Authorized in Commission and Manager forms (25% voter petition within 20 days suspends ordinance until voted upon).
